items.title: Cursor Cloud Agents can now run in Vercel Sandbox
items.excerpt: Vercel now lets Cursor Cloud Agents execute inside Vercel Sandbox — scale-to-zero workers, isolated microVMs and durable orchestration on infrastructure the team controls.
items.why: The coding agent stops being a laptop tool and becomes shared team infrastructure — design-to-code work can now run on the same preview pipeline the product ships from.

items.title: Agent-Native Clips: a free Loom alternative that captures browser errors
items.excerpt: Builder.io released an open-source screen recorder that records a browser bug together with console logs and failed network requests, producing a clip an agent can act on directly.
items.why: Designers file bugs by recording their screen; this turns that same recording into machine-readable evidence, closing the handoff gap between 'it looks broken' and a fix.

items.title: When the canvas starts acting, who's really in control?
items.excerpt: An argument that agentic canvases — surfaces that pull context across tools and then act without step-by-step instruction — change what designers actually control: interaction, agency, orchestration and attention.
items.why: Names the concrete design problem behind agentic UI: the canvas is no longer a passive surface, so control and reversibility become the thing you design.

items.title: AI took away engineering's right to say no
items.excerpt: Code complexity used to be both a wall and a gate: engineers were the only ones who could declare what was possible. AI didn't take their knowledge — it took that veto.
items.why: Directly reframes design-engineering power dynamics in AI teams — 'that's not feasible' stops being a conversation-ender for designers.

items.title: What Minority Report got right about AI
items.excerpt: Rereads Spielberg's Precogs as the sharpest portrait of generative AI drawn before it arrived — fluent, confident, acting on their own, hallucinations included — and asks what that means for the operator dwarfed by the machine.
items.why: A usable interface critique dressed as film analysis: the screen was never the subject, the operator's shrinking role was.

items.title: Three design-to-code hacks most developers ignore
items.excerpt: Argues the real losses in front-end work happen in the translation from design file to component, not in framework choice, and lays out three concrete habits that survive AI-assisted builds.
items.why: Practical craft-level guidance for the handoff step that AI tools most often get subtly wrong.

items.title: I let AI design tools build my portfolio site — clients noticed
items.excerpt: A first-person account of handing a portfolio build to AI design tools and measuring what clients actually reacted to — clarity of the three questions a portfolio must answer, not visual polish.
items.why: A rare before/after on AI-built design work judged by clients rather than by the builder.

items.title: Show rollback evidence before approving the agent rewrite
items.excerpt: The agent wants to delete the old settings path and you have forty seconds to say yes. A proposal for what proof an agent must surface before a human approves a destructive rewrite.
items.why: An approval-UI pattern for agentic tools: the design question is what evidence a confirmation dialog owes the person clicking it.

items.title: ArtStation enables NoAI protection for every artist by default
items.excerpt: ArtStation has switched NoAI protection on for new and existing uploads and added safeguards against AI crawlers, while admitting its current AI-content filters remain insufficient.
items.why: The largest portfolio platform for concept artists flips the default on training-data consent — a structural change to where creative work can be scraped.

items.title: ArtStation is taking action against AI art, but there's one question it won't answer
items.excerpt: Artists welcome ArtStation's new AI protections but press the platform on the thing it keeps avoiding: what happens to work already scraped, and how AI submissions are detected at all.
items.why: The artist-side reading of the same policy — the gap between a NoAI flag and actual enforcement is where creative trust is decided.

items.title: NVIDIA accelerates local AI at IFA 2026
items.excerpt: At IFA 2026 NVIDIA and partners showed faster local inference plus new tooling that makes agents easier to set up and run on-device across RTX and Spark hardware.
items.why: On-device agents change the economics of creative work — model runs stop metering per token and assets never leave the workstation.

items.title: Meet Lamp: an 'alive' Pixar-like desk robot that watches your posture
items.excerpt: A desk robot styled after the Pixar lamp that tracks posture, remembers faces it has seen and handles email — an embodied AI assistant whose whole interface is a physical gesture vocabulary.
items.why: A working example of embodied AI where the product design — motion, posture, character — is the entire interaction model.

items.title: SunCubes uses AI simulation to develop UAV charging systems
items.excerpt: SunCubes leaned on SimScale's AI-assisted thermal, structural and aerodynamic analysis to iterate wireless energy-transfer hardware without building each physical prototype.
items.why: Concrete hardware-design case where simulation replaces prototype rounds — the AX pattern industrial designers can copy.

items.title: Flying high at JetZero
items.excerpt: JetZero combines advanced modelling, simulation and AI to refine its blended-wing aircraft, using computation to attack engineering problems that have no reference design to copy.
items.why: Shows AI-assisted design doing its hardest job: shaping a form with no precedent, rather than optimising a known one.

items.title: Siemens Realize Live 2026
items.excerpt: Siemens' Xcelerator push gained momentum across its global events, with new features and partnerships aimed at making the CAD-to-manufacturing chain AI-assisted end to end.
items.why: Reads how the biggest industrial-design toolchain is positioning AI — relevant to any team whose design work ends in a factory.

items.title: AI ruined posters. This human designer is fixing them
items.excerpt: Bad AI-designed posters have become common enough that a human graphic designer is redesigning them publicly — unnatural sheen, yellowish cast and mangled type included — to show what a living designer's touch still buys.
items.why: A visible, teachable diagnostic of AI output failure modes, argued in the medium designers actually judge: the poster.

items.title: Man City fans used AI to design the team's new kit
items.excerpt: Manchester City's new alternative kit is the first professional football kit designed by fans using generative AI — made with Puma AI Creator, the brand's custom tool — and it will be worn on the pitch.
items.why: Generative AI crosses from concept render into a manufactured, licensed product: a real test of who holds authorship in brand design.

items.title: Worried your writing sounds like AI? These tools can help
items.excerpt: AI-generated prose now fills LinkedIn, Substack, medical papers and published books — and a crop of tools has appeared to detect and strip the tells out of your own drafts.
items.why: UX copy and brand voice are design surfaces too; the 'sounds like AI' tell is becoming a measurable quality defect.

items.title: OpenAI's next big AI model has 'entered the AGI era'
items.excerpt: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says the company's next flagship model marks entry into the AGI era, framing the release around capability claims rather than benchmarks.
items.why: The frontier model most creative tools will sit on next — worth reading for what actually ships versus what is claimed.

items.title: The most overhyped and underhyped new AI models
items.excerpt: A hands-on sort through the current wave of new model releases, separating the ones that change day-to-day creative work from the ones that only look good in launch demos.
items.why: Useful triage for designers deciding which of this month's model launches is worth rebuilding a workflow around.

items.title: 5 skills that make ChatGPT and Claude better at everything
items.excerpt: A walkthrough of five reusable skills that measurably improve output quality from ChatGPT and Claude, aimed at people who want leverage rather than another prompt list.
items.why: Skills are becoming the packaging format for repeatable creative workflows — this is the practical version of that shift.

items.title: The mystery is solved... and the answer is 40x cheaper than Claude
items.excerpt: Fireship traces the anonymous model that appeared on the leaderboards and lands on the cost story: comparable output at roughly a fortieth of the price.
items.why: Token price is what decides whether an agentic design workflow is affordable to run continuously.
